arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Utah's counsel stated the census has historically used an actual count without statistical estimation.
North Carolina's counsel argued the right time to challenge census methods is before the census completes.
The Solicitor General noted the Census Bureau used imputation for missing data in the last five censuses.
Utah's counsel clarified the record does not show most imputations occurred in known occupied units.

paragraphs: How could a state challenge imputation figures before knowing they caused a problem?

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines when states can legally challenge census statistical methods. It defines the scope of judicial review for population counting procedures. The outcome shapes the balance between statistical accuracy and constitutional counting requirements.
